headline: A reproducible benchmark now lets materials scientists test agents on real computational workflows.
summary_for_scientists: CompMat-Bench turns computational materials studies into reproducible tasks with reference outputs and fixed-rule grading. Alongside new chemistry perspectives and agent-evaluation tools, the week offers a practical lab-meeting prompt: which parts of a materials workflow can an agent complete reliably today?

lab_pick.title: CompMat-Bench: benchmark agents on real computational materials workflows
lab_pick.what_they_did: The authors built 94 tasks from published computational-materials studies, reproduced the task steps in advance, and graded agents against reference results with fixed rules.
lab_pick.result: Across three LLM-based agents, pass rates on single tasks with full methodological guidance ranged from 66.0% to 90.4%; longer workflows and less guidance affected results differently.
lab_pick.why_researchers_care: This is a concrete test of scientific work rather than a general reasoning quiz. The task structure and fixed grading make it possible to discuss what an agent can execute in a computational materials workflow.
lab_pick.how_to_share: Share the benchmark in a lab meeting, choose one task that resembles the group's work, and discuss what evidence would count as a successful reproduction.
